title: Unbalanced Growth and Land Overvaluation
core_object: Land overvaluation theorem; land as store of value under unbalanced growth
main_mechanism: When non-land sectors experience faster technological progress and substitution elasticity between land and non-land factors exceeds one, land prices can rise above rent fundamentals even as land’s production role declines.
project_role: Core theorem for the review; explains land overvaluation through unbalanced growth rather than irrational exuberance.

title: Land and Infinite Debt Rollover
core_object: Infinite debt rollover in OLG economy with land
main_mechanism: Unbalanced growth weakens the standard land-economy result that R>G blocks Ponzi rollover; land bubbles can coexist with Pareto efficiency and debt rollover.
project_role: Core source for debt rollover question and critique of R versus G reasoning when land is present.

title: Credit, Land Speculation, and Low-Interest-Rate Policy
core_object: Low interest rates, credit composition, land speculation, long-run growth
main_mechanism: Credit expansions tied to real estate financing and low-rate policy redirect savings toward land speculation, crowding out productive capital investment and reducing long-term productivity growth.
project_role: Core source for credit expansion and interest-rate policy mechanisms.

title: Growth and Fluctuations Economies with Land Speculation
core_object: Overview of OLG global dynamics with land, credit frictions, endogenous growth
main_mechanism: Land introduces an alternative store of value and amplifies nonlinear rational-expectations dynamics, producing bounded but persistent fluctuations and possible stagnation traps.
project_role: Bridge paper that summarizes the research program and connects wobbly dynamics, land speculation, and credit.

title: Henry George, Land Speculation, and Economic Growth and Transformation
core_object: Land speculation, land taxation, growth, institutional arrangements
main_mechanism: Land speculation diverts savings away from productive capital; land taxes, rent taxation, and public ownership/nationalization can mitigate growth-retarding speculation.
project_role: Policy and institutional anchor; useful for connecting theory to land reform, taxation, and regulation.

title: The Wobbly Economy: Global Dynamics with Phase and State Transitions
core_object: Wobbly macro-dynamics without land as baseline global-dynamics framework
main_mechanism: Multiplicity of momentary equilibria in a life-cycle model can generate bounded non-convergent rational-expectations paths, phase transitions, and hysteresis.
project_role: Theoretical baseline for understanding the later land-speculation models.

title: Land Speculation and Wobbly Dynamics with Endogenous Phase Transitions
core_object: Land speculation and endogenous boom-bust dynamics
main_mechanism: Land prices interact with capital accumulation; rising land prices crowd out productive capital and can trigger endogenous phase transitions between unique and multiple equilibria.
project_role: Core dynamic model for real-estate booms, busts, and rational land-price fluctuations.

authors: Tomohiro Hirano; Ryo Jinnai; Alexis Akira Toda
title: Leverage, Endogenous Unbalanced Growth, and Asset Price Bubbles
core_object: Leverage threshold, phase transition, unbalanced growth, land bubbles
main_mechanism: Relaxed leverage strengthens the feedback loop between land prices and capital investment; beyond a critical threshold, the economy shifts from balanced fundamental valuation to unbalanced bubbly growth.
project_role: Formal bridge between finance, leverage, and unbalanced growth; complements the Land Overvaluation Theorem.

title: The Measurement of Wealth: Recessions, Sustainability and Inequality
core_object: Wealth measurement, sustainability, land rents, missing capital
main_mechanism: Measured wealth can rise through capitalized rents, especially land, without any increase in productive capacity; downturns can destroy unmeasured productive potential.
project_role: Measurement foundation for distinguishing land-value inflation from productive-capacity formation.

title: New Theoretical Perspectives on the Distribution of Income and Wealth among Individuals: Part IV: Land and Credit
main_mechanism: Land-price increases, bubbles, collateral rules, and lower interest rates can raise measured wealth and inequality while crowding out real capital accumulation.
project_role: Pre-Hirano/Stiglitz foundation for linking land, credit, wealth inequality, and financial policy.

title: New Theoretical Perspectives on the Distribution of Income and Wealth among Individuals: Part I. The Wealth Residual
core_object: Wealth residual; capital versus wealth; rents
main_mechanism: The rise in wealth-income ratios cannot be explained by saving alone; land rents, exploitation rents, and intellectual-property rents help explain divergence between wealth and productive capital.
project_role: Conceptual starting point for why land-price capitalization matters for distribution and measurement.

title: Land Bubbles Despite Non-Vanishing Rents
core_object: Land bubbles with constant housing rent yield
main_mechanism: Separating pure land rent from rent on housing structures shows that land bubbles can exist even when observed housing rent-to-price ratios appear stationary.
project_role: Measurement warning: do not infer absence of land bubbles from aggregate housing rent yields.

title: Credit, Land Speculation, and Long-Run Economic Growth
core_object: Sectoral credit expansion, real-estate finance, long-run growth
main_mechanism: Credit to construction/real estate predicts productivity and growth slowdowns, while credit to manufacturing is growth-enhancing; land speculation can crowd out productive investment.
project_role: Core paper for task items 2.1 and 2.2; probably the main technical source before policy-updated versions.

title: Land, G versus R, and Infinite Debt Rollover
core_object: Land, R versus G, debt rollover, unbalanced growth
main_mechanism: The land economy changes the theoretical meaning of R versus G; balanced growth tends to restore R>G, while unbalanced growth can permit debt rollover and land bubbles.
project_role: Latest CIGS version for debt-rollover synthesis; compare against PDF002.
